ref: Check for causes of decreased consciousness (check_for)
text: The pupil branch is incomplete: 'Unequal or respond poorly to light' is a red-box finding with its own escalation ('Discuss urgently with referral centre') and is neither checked for nor used. Will's briefing requires every red-box item in the check_for. Candidate concepts exist: (snomed_concept "Anisocoria" "disorder"), (snomed_concept "Sluggish pupil movement" "finding"), (snomed_concept "Abnormal pupil reaction" "finding").

Only one priority level (Urgent) for every patient. The page's deterioration criteria (BP < 90/60, pulse > 100 or < 50, RR > 20 or < 9, SpO2 < 94%) in a patient with decreased consciousness match Will's named example for Very urgent / Emergency ('BP < 90/60 with altered consciousness'); the unequal/poorly-reactive-pupil branch ('Discuss urgently') is another escalation. Neither is encoded, so the file cannot distinguish a stable from a deteriorating unconscious patient.

ref: Whole file: glucose and temperature branches
text: Of the page's seven leaf thresholds under 'Check glucose, temperature and pupils', only >= 11.1 (as a gate), >= 38°C, pinpoint and both-dilated are encoded. Glucose < 3 (< 4 if diabetes), temperature <= 35°C and the unequal/poorly reactive pupils are absent. The builders encoded >= 38°C as a possible diagnosis even though the page only says 'for possible meningitis' in a drug instruction, so the same reasoning should have produced possible Hypoglycemia (with (active_condition Diabetes mellitus) raising the cut-off to 4) and possible Hypothermia, or the remaining-questions file should say why not.

ref: Diagnose probable shock with decreased consciousness and glucose >= 11.1
text: The shock criteria are gated on glucose >= 11.1 because the box sits under that branch. This is faithful to the layout, but it means an unconscious patient with SBP < 80 and glucose 6 gets no shock diagnosis from this page. Also the page's comma list ('SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, respiratory rate > 30, weakness') is read as any-of; it may mean the combination. Both choices are defensible; they should be recorded as judgement calls.

ref: Diagnose probable shock / Diagnose probable poisoning / Diagnose possible meningitis (measurement concepts)
text: Pulse is measured as (snomed_concept "Pulse, function" "observable entity"), whose parent is 'Cardiovascular function', not a rate; (snomed_concept "Heart rate" "observable entity") is the natural concept for a bpm value. Glucose is measured as (snomed_concept "Blood glucose status" "observable entity") (parent 'General clinical state'); (snomed_concept "Blood glucose concentration" "observable entity") is the natural concept for a mmol/L value. If the recorded vitals use the other concepts these comparisons never match and the rules silently never fire. I could not see the vitals anchor, so this is a flag, not a confirmed error.

ref: Diagnose probable poisoning with decreased consciousness
text: Pinpoint pupils alone do not reach 'Poisoning likely'; the rule requires one of illicit drug use, RR < 12, excessive secretions or muscle twitching as well. On the page the two sub-boxes hang off 'Pinpoint' as the two poisoning patterns and the 'Poisoning likely' bar sits under the whole pinpoint column, so pinpoint pupils in an unconscious adult are arguably sufficient. A judgement call; the stricter reading loses the case of pinpoint pupils with no other feature.

'If patient was in malaria area in past 3 months, manage 39' under the >= 38°C branch is an implied 'consider malaria' and is not encoded. SNOMED as searched has no malaria-area exposure concept, so this may be a not_representable gap, but it should be recorded.
